introduction: Steadfastness is called in these passages the crown of all deeds: to remain firm in faith and unswerving in love when tests come, when others fall away, and when there is nothing to show for one's effort. The readings define it, liken it to a mountain and a deep-rooted tree, connect it with patience, love, faithfulness to the Covenant and trust in God, tell of people who stood firm, and end in prayers to be kept from slipping. A hundred voices stand beside them: the Psalms and prophets, the Gospels and letters, the Qur’an's prayers for a sure foothold, Confucius and the Dhammapada, Marcus Aurelius and Seneca, Polycarp, Shakespeare, Milton, Tennyson and Kipling, with Emerson and Job to ask what firmness is not.
questions: Emerson scorned "a foolish consistency." How do these passages distinguish steadfastness from stubbornness or habit?
The mountain, the rock and the rooted tree recur here and in the Psalms, Marcus Aurelius and the Dhammapada. What does each image say that the others do not?
Confucius says the cold shows which trees keep their leaves. Do tests make a person steadfast, or show what was already there?
Shakespeare's Caesar boasts of being constant as the northern star. Where do these readings place the source of firmness?
The father in Mark says "I believe; help thou mine unbelief," and Tennyson defends honest doubt. Is doubt the opposite of steadfastness?
The last two sections are prayers. Why should steadfastness, of all virtues, be something to pray for and not only to resolve upon?

outside.why: Paul asks the same of the Corinthians: be steadfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work.
Emerson called a foolish consistency the hobgoblin of little minds and said a great soul has nothing to do with it. How is being unswerving in love different from the consistency he scorned?
This is the verse quoted: on those who say "Our Lord is God" and then stay upright, the angels descend.
Jesus tells of a merchant who sold everything for one pearl, a jewel beyond the price of all the rest.
Jesus warns that the love of many will grow cold, and says that the one who endures to the end will be saved.
The letter of James promises a crown of life to the one who endures trial.
Paul's closing charge to Corinth is brief: watch, stand fast in the faith, be strong.
The Revelation of John gives the promise in one line: be faithful unto death, and I will give you a crown of life.
Paul says that what is prepared for those who love God has not been seen or heard or imagined.
Milton's Abdiel is the type of this firmness: faithful among the faithless, unmoved by numbers or example.
Jesus says that whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much.
Jesus says that no one who puts a hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom.
A father cries out to Jesus: I believe; help my unbelief. Can a person be steadfast and still need to pray those words?
Jesus compares the one who hears and does to a house built on rock, which the storm cannot bring down.
A psalmist gives the same rule: I have set the Lord always before me, and so I shall not be moved.
Isaiah promises perfect peace to the one whose mind is stayed on God, the everlasting strength.
Paul, warned of chains ahead, answers that none of these things move him if only he may finish his course.
A psalm uses the same image: those who trust are like Mount Zion, which cannot be removed.
Marcus Aurelius tells himself to be like the headland on which the waves break and which stands firm.
The Dhammapada says that the wise are no more shaken by blame and praise than a solid rock is by the wind.
The first psalm pictures the faithful as a tree planted by rivers of water, whose leaf does not wither.
Jeremiah draws the same tree, which does not fear when heat comes and does not cease to bear fruit.
Isaiah hears a promise from God's side that matches this covenant: the mountains may depart, but my kindness will not.
Shakespeare's Caesar boasts that he is as constant as the northern star, moments before he falls. What separates the constancy asked for here from pride in one's own firmness?
A psalm says the same of the direst calamity: we will not fear though the earth be removed.
The letter of James likens the waverer to a wave of the sea, driven and tossed by the wind.
Paul warns against being children carried about by every wind of doctrine.
Peter compares tested faith to gold that is proved in the fire.
Seneca has the same proverb: fire tries gold, and misfortune tries the brave.
The apostles left the council rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer.
Confucius remarks that only when the year turns cold do we learn that the pine and cypress keep their leaves. Do tests create steadfastness, or reveal it?
Jesus tells Peter that he is to be sifted like wheat, and that he has prayed for his faith not to fail.
The psalm that Jesus quotes from the cross asks why God has forsaken him. Is trembling in the wind of tests a failure of steadfastness, or part of it?
Kipling's advice to a son is to meet triumph and disaster and treat both impostors alike.
Jesus describes the hearer without root who endures for a while and falls away when trouble comes.
The letter of James points to the prophets and to Job as examples of patience under suffering.
The phrase "beautiful patience" is Jacob's, in the Qur’an, when his sons bring him Joseph's shirt.
The Qur’an calls on believers to endure, to outdo all others in endurance, and to stand ready.
A psalm tells the faithful not to fret because of evildoers, who are soon cut down.
Paul glories in tribulation because it produces patience, and patience experience, and experience hope.
Jesus in Gethsemane prayed that the cup might pass from him, and then accepted it. Is a longing for tribulation asked of everyone, or is his prayer also a pattern?
Milton, going blind, concludes that those also serve who only stand and wait. Is waiting a form of steadfastness, or its hardest test?
Paul says that those who are comforted in affliction become able to comfort others.
The Song of Songs gives love the same sign: it is strong as death, and floods cannot drown it.
Shakespeare defines love as an ever-fixed mark that looks on tempests and is never shaken.
Paul is persuaded that neither death nor life nor any power can separate us from the love of God.
A psalm speaks for those who can say: for thy sake we are killed all the day long.
Jeremiah found the word a burning fire shut up in his bones that he could not hold in.
Jesus calls blessed those who are reviled and persecuted for his sake.
Ruth's words to Naomi are the classic vow of a love that will not be turned back.
The risen Jesus asks Peter three times whether he loves him, once for each denial.
Jesus tells his disciples to abide in him as branches abide in the vine.
Paul asks his readers to arm themselves so that, having done all, they may stand.
The letter to the Hebrews urges holding fast without wavering, because the one who promised is faithful.
Deuteronomy calls God the faithful God who keeps covenant to a thousand generations.
Jesus, before leaving his disciples, tells them not to let their hearts be troubled.
The Qur’an has the same image of a cord: hold fast, all together, to the cable of God.
Aesop's father shows his sons that sticks bound together cannot be broken.
In the parable the master's praise is for faithfulness: well done, good and faithful servant.
The Qur’an honours those who were true to what they covenanted with God and did not alter.
The Revelation of John praises a church for its patience and labour and then says it has left its first love. Can a person be faithful in works and not in love?
Jesus says that a tree is known by its fruits, the test this passage applies to faith.
Proverbs says that a friend loves at all times and a brother is born for adversity.
Lamentations says of God what is said here of a servant: his faithfulness is new every morning.
Paul sums up his life: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.
Paul tells the Galatians not to grow weary, for in due season they will reap.
Lincoln asked his nation for firmness in the right and for striving on to finish the work.
The letter to the Hebrews pictures life as a race to be run with patience to its finish.
Tennyson's Ulysses resolves to strive, to seek, to find and not to yield, on the strength of his own will. On what does perseverance rest in these letters?
Paul forgets what is behind, reaches for what is ahead and presses toward the mark.
Longfellow's psalm of life ends: still achieving, still pursuing, learn to labour and to wait.
Proverbs says that a just man falls seven times and rises again.
Isaiah promises that those who wait on the Lord shall renew their strength.
Proverbs gives the rule of trust: lean not on your own understanding, and he will direct your paths.
At the end of the book of Job, God says that Job, who protested, spoke rightly. How does contentment with what God ordains leave room for Job's kind of speech?
Epictetus gives the Stoic form of contentment: wish things to happen as they do happen.
Nehemiah's builders prayed to God and also set a watch day and night. How do trust and effort belong together in this passage?
The Qur’an promises a way out and provision from an unexpected quarter to the one who trusts.
Isaiah's servant says: I have set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed.
Socrates tells his judges that he will obey God rather than them and will not stop while he has breath.
Confucius says that an army may lose its commander, but the will of even a common man cannot be taken from him.
Stephen died praying for those who were stoning him, and held no grievance against them.
The letter to the Hebrews remembers those who wandered in deserts and mountains, of whom the world was not worthy.
Three young men answer a king that their God can deliver them, and that even if he does not they will not yield.
Jeremiah hears Rachel weeping for her children and refusing to be comforted. What did it cost this mother to speak to her son as she did?
The aged Polycarp, told to renounce his Lord, replied that he had served him eighty-six years and received no wrong.
The Qur’an recalls the devoted companions of earlier prophets, who did not weaken or give in under what befell them.
Paul lists his own years of beatings, shipwreck and dangers on the road.
A psalm sees the sparrow find a house and the swallow a nest at the altars of God.
A psalmist tells how he was lifted from the pit and his feet set upon a rock.
A psalm has the same prayer: hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not.
The Qur’an teaches the prayer: Our Lord, let not our hearts stray after thou hast guided us.
The letter of Jude ends by praising the one who is able to keep us from falling.
A psalm asks for a right spirit to be renewed within, and to be upheld.
In the Qur’an those who faced Goliath prayed for endurance and a sure foothold.
In the Qur’an the magicians of Pharaoh, threatened with death, ask only for constancy to be poured out on them.
The Qur’an says that God confirms believers with a firm word in this life and the next.
Tennyson wrote that there lives more faith in honest doubt than in half the creeds. Is every doubt a hindrance to be prayed against?
Paul and Barnabas told their converts to continue in the faith through many tribulations.
A psalmist says that though flesh and heart fail, God is his portion for ever.

corinthians-quit-you-like-men.text: Watch ye, stand fast in the faith, quit you like men, be strong

ephesians-having-done-all-to-stand.text: Wherefore take unto you the whole armour of God, that ye may be able to withstand in the evil day, and having done all, to stand

matthew-house-upon-a-rock.text: Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man, which built his house upon a rock

matthew-endureth-to-the-end.text: And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved

james-endureth-temptation.text: Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them that love him

hebrews-without-wavering.text: Let us hold fast the profession of our faith without wavering; (for he is faithful that promised

hebrews-run-with-patience.text: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us, Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith

psalm-as-mount-zion.text: They that trust in the Lord shall be as mount Zion, which cannot be removed, but abideth for ever

psalm-heart-is-fixed.text: Surely he shall not be moved for ever: the righteous shall be in everlasting remembrance. He shall not be afraid of evil tidings: his heart is fixed, trusting in the Lord

isaiah-mind-is-stayed.text: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee. Trust ye in the Lord for ever: for in the Lord Jehovah is everlasting strength

isaiah-mountains-shall-depart.text: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the Lord that hath mercy on thee

proverbs-trust-in-the-lord.text: Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding. In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths

psalm-commit-thy-way.text: Commit thy way unto the Lord; trust also in him; and he shall bring it to pass

peter-resist-stedfast.text: Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour: Whom resist stedfast in the faith, knowing that the same afflictions are accomplished in your brethren that are in the world

james-wave-of-the-sea.text: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed. For let not that man think that he shall receive any thing of the Lord. A double minded man is unstable in all his ways

ephesians-every-wind-of-doctrine.text: That we henceforth be no more children, tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive

isaiah-face-like-a-flint.text: For the Lord God will help me; therefore shall I not be confounded: therefore have I set my face like a flint, and I know that I shall not be ashamed

acts-none-of-these-things-move-me.text: But none of these things move me, neither count I my life dear unto myself, so that I might finish my course with joy, and the ministry, which I have received of the Lord Jesus, to testify the gospel of the grace of God

acts-stephen-fell-asleep.text: And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep

psalm-footsteps-slip-not.text: Hold up my goings in thy paths, that my footsteps slip not

luke-that-thy-faith-fail-not.text: And the Lord said, Simon, Simon, behold, Satan hath desired to have you, that he may sift you as wheat: But I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not: and when thou art converted, strengthen thy brethren

jude-keep-you-from-falling.text: Now unto him that is able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory with exceeding joy, To the only wise God our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and ever. Amen

psalm-feet-upon-a-rock.text: I waited patiently for the Lord; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings

mark-help-thou-mine-unbelief.text: And straightway the father of the child cried out, and said with tears, Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief

proverbs-falleth-seven-times.text: For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again: but the wicked shall fall into mischief

job-shall-we-not-receive-evil.text: Then said his wife unto him, Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die. But he said unto her, Thou speakest as one of the foolish women speaketh. What? shall we receive good at the hand of God, and shall we not receive evil? In all this did not Job sin with his lips

quran-angels-descend-upon-them.text: Lo! those who say: Our Lord is Allah, and afterward are upright, the angels descend upon them, saying: Fear not nor grieve, but hear good tidings of the paradise which ye are promised.

quran-endure-outdo-in-endurance.text: O ye who believe! Endure, outdo all others in endurance, be ready, and observe your duty to Allah, in order that ye may succeed.

quran-quailed-not.text: And with how many a prophet have there been a number of devoted men who fought (beside him). They quailed not for aught that befell them in the way of Allah, nor did they weaken, nor were they brought low. Allah loveth the steadfast.

quran-tread-the-straight-path.text: So tread thou the straight path as thou art commanded, and those who turn (unto Allah) with thee, and transgress not. Lo! He is Seer of what ye do.

quran-steadfast-heart-of-things.text: O my dear son! Establish worship and enjoin kindness and forbid iniquity, and persevere whatever may befall thee. Lo! that is of the steadfast heart of things.

quran-firm-saying.text: Allah confirmeth those who believe by a firm saying in the life of the world and in the Hereafter, and Allah sendeth wrong-doers astray. And Allah doeth what He will.

quran-hearts-stray-not.text: Our Lord! Cause not our hearts to stray after Thou hast guided us, and bestow upon us mercy from Thy Presence. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Bestower.

quran-foothold-sure.text: And when they went into the field against Goliath and his hosts they said: Our Lord! Bestow on us endurance, make our foothold sure, and give us help against the disbelieving folk.

quran-pour-out-constancy.text: Thou takest vengeance on us only forasmuch as we believed the tokens of our Lord when they came unto us. Our Lord! Vouchsafe unto us steadfastness and make us die as men who have surrendered (unto Thee).

shakespeare-constant-as-the-northern-sta.text: But I am constant as the northern star, / Of whose true-fix'd and resting quality / There is no fellow in the firmament
shakespeare-constant-as-the-northern-sta.author: William Shakespeare

source.label: The Complete Works of William Shakespeare (MIT)

analects-will-of-a-common-man.text: The commander of the forces of a large state may be carried off, but the will of even a common man cannot be taken from him
analects-will-of-a-common-man.author: Confucius

analects-pine-and-cypress.text: When the year becomes cold, then we know how the pine and the cypress are the last to lose their leaves
analects-pine-and-cypress.author: Confucius

dhammapada-solid-rock.text: As a solid rock is not shaken by the wind, wise people falter not amidst blame and praise

polycarp-eighty-and-six-years.text: Eighty and six years have I served Him, and He never did me any injury: how then can I blaspheme my King and my Saviour

emerson-foolish-consistency.text: A foolish consistency is the hobgoblin of little minds, adored by little statesmen and philosophers and divines. With consistency a great soul has simply nothing to do
emerson-foolish-consistency.author: Ralph Waldo Emerson

psalm-lord-always-before-me.text: I have set the Lord always before me: because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved
